Simultaneous credible intervals and joint directional statements

Source: R/joint.R
joint.Rd

Two ways of making directional claims about several parameters from their joint posterior. By default, joint() returns simultaneous credible intervals. With interval = FALSE it returns, for each \(k\), the joint posterior probability that the \(k\) strongest directional claims all hold.

Usage

joint(
  draws,
  interval = TRUE,
  prob = 0.95,
  null.value = 0,
  direction = NULL,
  est.FUN = median
)

Arguments

draws

Matrix or data frame of posterior draws, one column per parameter, with at least 1000 rows and 2 columns.

interval

Logical. If TRUE (the default), simultaneous credible intervals are returned. If FALSE, the joint directional statement.

prob

Number in \((0, 1)\). Joint posterior probability of the intervals. Defaults to 0.95. Used only when interval = TRUE.

null.value

Number or vector, the null value of each parameter. A single number applies to all parameters. Defaults to 0. Used only when interval = FALSE.

direction

Character vector with elements "two.sided", "greater", or "less", one per parameter, or a single value for all. NULL (the default) means "two.sided" for all, that is, the side favored by the posterior. Used only when interval = FALSE.

est.FUN

Function that computes a point estimate from the draws of one parameter. Defaults to median. Used only when interval = TRUE.

Value

A data frame with one row per parameter and a print method. With interval = TRUE, an object of class joint_interval with the columns lower, est, upper, and prob. With interval = FALSE, an object of class joint_directional, sorted by decreasing pd, with the columns median.est, null.value, pd, direction, and joint_cum.

Details

Simultaneous credible intervals (interval = TRUE). Equal-tailed intervals such that all parameters lie inside their interval at the same time with posterior probability prob. For every draw, the function takes the smallest tail probability across parameters, and the intervals are set at the \((1 - \texttt{prob})\)-quantile of these values. A direction can be claimed for a parameter when its interval excludes the null value.

The ends of the intervals lie further in the tails as the number of parameters grows, so more draws are needed. Each end rests on about \(S (1 - \texttt{prob}^{1/m}) / 2\) draws, where \(S\) is the number of draws and \(m\) the number of parameters. With fewer than 10, the intervals are too narrow on average and joint() gives a warning. With prob = 0.95, this means at least about 1,600 draws for 4 parameters, 7,800 for 20, and 15,600 for 40. sim.cred.band in the credsubs package (Schnell et al., 2020) is a closely related implementation.

Joint directional statement (interval = FALSE). The direction of each parameter is the side of null.value favored by its posterior, or the side given in direction. Parameters are sorted by decreasing pd, and joint_cum gives, for each \(k\), the proportion of draws in which the first \(k\) directions all hold. It therefore accounts for the posterior dependence among parameters. This is a probability about the signs of the parameters under the prior of the fitted model, with no adjustment of the prior odds. In families with many null effects it leads to many false claims.

References

Box, G. E. P., & Tiao, G. C. (1992). Bayesian inference in statistical analysis (1st ed.). Wiley.

Besag, J., Green, P., Higdon, D., & Mengersen, K. (1995). Bayesian computation and stochastic systems. Statistical Science, 10(1), 3–41.

Held, L. (2004). Simultaneous posterior probability statements from Monte Carlo output. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 13(1), 20–35.

Gelman, A., Tuerlinckx, F. (2000). Type S error rates for classical and Bayesian single and multiple comparison procedures. Computational Statistics 15, 373–390 (2000). https://doi.org/10.1007/s001800000040

Schnell, P. et al. (2020). credsubs: Credible Subsets. R package. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=credsubs.

See also

pd.adjust for the per-test prior-odds threshold.

Examples

mu <- c(1.5, 0, -2)
Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.5, 0.8, 1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3, 1), 3, 3)
draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(2000, mu, Sigma)
colnames(draws) <- c("theta1", "theta2", "theta3")

joint(draws)                     # simultaneous credible intervals (default)
#> Simultaneous credible intervals (joint probability 0.95)
#> 
#>          lower     est  upper
#> theta1 -0.7416  1.4721 3.8524
#> theta2 -2.3636 -0.0241 2.1471
#> theta3 -4.3930 -1.9897 0.3948
joint(draws, interval = FALSE)   # joint directional statement
#> Joint directional statement
#>   null value = 0, direction = two.sided
#>   joint_cum: Pr(the top k claims all hold | y)
#> 
#>        median.est     pd joint_cum
#> theta3    -1.9897 0.9750    0.9750
#> theta1     1.4721 0.9360    0.9115
#> theta2    -0.0241 0.5095    0.4415
